entries.title: Loren talks back — voice output (OpenAI TTS)
bullets: Completed the voice loop: a speaker toggle in the session header makes Loren read her replies aloud (OpenAI gpt-4o-mini-tts, warm voice). Talk to her, she talks back — the ChatGPT-voice experience, all on your OpenAI key.
Every AI reply also has a small Play button so you can hear any one on demand; markdown/HTML is stripped so she never reads asterisks or tags out loud.
The on/off preference is remembered; each spoken reply logs a small voice_out micro-credit to Activity/ledger.
New loren-speak edge function; reuses your OpenAI key — no extra setup.
entries.bench: loren-speak (gpt-4o-mini-tts) · useLorenSpeech · header toggle + per-reply Play · voice_out micro-credit

entries.title: Clear Live vs Recording indicator in the composer
bullets: Both composers now show a green ● Live pill (streaming word-by-word, with a live transcript preview) or a red ● Recording pill (record-then-transcribe), plus timer — so it's obvious which voice mode is active.
entries.bench: VoiceStatus pill · live preview · home + session composers

entries.title: OpenAI Realtime live voice — words as you speak, on your OpenAI key
bullets: OpenAI Realtime transcription (gpt-4o-transcribe over WebRTC): words stream in live as you speak, then the clean transcript lands in the box. Falls back to record-then-transcribe if Realtime can't connect.
Ephemeral token minted server-side (loren-realtime-token) — your OpenAI key is never exposed. Voice micro-crediting: 1 credit per started minute, logged to Activity.
entries.bench: loren-realtime-token · useLorenVoice WebRTC live → batch fallback · voice micro-crediting

entries.title: Voice-to-text → OpenAI-only
bullets: Replaced the flaky browser mic with OpenAI gpt-4o-transcribe (any-length, clean text); briefly trialed Deepgram then settled OpenAI-only on your key.
